speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me. To begin our discussion regarding your headache and worsening vision over the past three weeks, could you please describe the specific character of your pain and exactly what visual changes you are experiencing?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age and the progressive nature of your headache with vision changes, have you noticed any specific visual disturbances, such as blurriness, double vision, or a dark curtain over your vision?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming. Given your age and the subacute progression of headache with worsening vision, have you noticed any visual field defects like a "curtain" coming down, or any double vision when looking in different directions? Also, do you experience any scalp tenderness or jaw pain while chewing?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient has hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She also has a history of high cholesterol. Social history: Retired school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate) and CRP (C-Reactive Protein). REQUEST IMAGES: Ophthalmoscopy. In the meantime, have you noticed any jaw pain while chewing or scalp tenderness when brushing your hair?

text: RESULTS: ESR: 45 mm/hr; CRP: 12 mg/L; Ophthalmoscopy: Shows dilated tortuous retinal veins with multiple intraretinal hemorrhages and cotton wool spots, consistent with bilateral retinal vein occlusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis) with secondary Bilateral Retinal Vein Occlusion.

The combination of your age, subacute headache, vision loss, elevated inflammatory markers (ESR 45, CRP 12), and the specific finding of bilateral retinal vein occlusion is highly indicative of vasculitis affecting the ophthalmic arteries and veins. We must immediately start you on high-dose corticosteroids to prevent permanent blindness in the fellow eye.
